result.title: Next Token or Vector? Learning How Far to Decode
result.summary: Standard autoregressive decoding advances one token at a time, even when several upcoming tokens can be predicted together. We propose CADENCE (Context-Adaptive DEcoding), a generation method that learns both what to draft and how far to draft. Gaussian prediction heads represent future spans as continuous latent vectors, and a shared decoder converts the selected vector into token predictions in parallel. A learned router selects the prediction length from the model's own hidden states and predicted Gaussian parameters, adapting generation granularity to the current context with single-token generation as a fallback. The backbone verifies each proposed continuation and retains the prefix that matches its greedy predictions. Experiments with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct on Alpaca, GSM8K, and HumanEval show that router-selected positions yield higher draft acceptance than applying the corresponding prediction length everywhere. CADENCE achieves up to 1.3x higher generation throughput than standard greedy decoding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CADENCE，用高斯预测头把未来若干 token 的片段编码为连续 latent 向量，共享解码器并行转成 token 预测，并由学习到的 router 依据隐藏状态与高斯参数决定每次草拟的长度，主干再验证并保留与贪心预测一致的前缀；在 Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 上测试 Alpaca、GSM8K、HumanEval，吞吐最高提升约 1.3 倍。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本工作，但「latent 向量刻画未来片段 + 由隐藏状态学习决定生成多远 + 验证保留」的机制，可能与 LVR 中动态计算、停止/长度决策以及 latent 状态筛选与验证的线索相关，可供核查其 router 信号能否迁移到多模态推理解码。
